sceneData.name: Central Lodge — B1 Cellar & Utility Basement

behaviorSpec.message: You recover the Rail Proof: physical evidence that the Lodge's utility infrastructure connects to a concealed railway system.

specification.failureHint: The pipework and drainage channels seem to converge on the same machinery.
specification.successHint: The flooded system is controlled from this spindle assembly, but a removable control component is missing.

behaviorSpec.successMessage: The basement machinery forms one connected water-control system. The wheel mounted at the control assembly is a removable component, while the drainage channels and flooded lower works answer to the same machinery.
behaviorSpec.criticalClueFallback: Deliberate inspection of the control machinery reveals that the mounted wheel can be detached.

specification.failureHint: Some maintenance marks and fittings do not match ordinary cellar work.
specification.successHint: The hardware includes standardized rail-service fittings and maintenance evidence from a system larger than this basement.

behaviorSpec.successMessage: Among the maintenance debris is something that does not belong to ordinary cellar work: old railway-related hardware and markings, handled often enough to suggest deliberate estate use rather than discarded scrap.
behaviorSpec.criticalClueFallback: A deliberate search of the maintenance evidence can still recover the physical railway proof.

behaviors.name: DiceBox B1 Water Control Wheel Recovery

behaviorSpec.message: You detach and recover the Water Control Wheel from the basement machinery.

sceneData.name: Central Lodge — B2 Hidden Annex & Sacrificial Preparation Area

specification.failureHint: The drainage and storage arrangement feels wrong for ordinary cellar work.
specification.successHint: The stains, restraint fittings, and drainage pattern are consistent with repeated preparation of bound victims rather than household maintenance.

specification.failureHint: Some work surfaces look less neglected than the surrounding stone.
specification.successHint: A few preparation surfaces, drains, and tools show repeated practical use that is much more recent than the room around them.

sceneData.name: Central Lodge — C1 Hidden Chapel / Shrine of Asmodeus

specification.failureHint: The shrine looks deliberately unfinished in a way ordinary damage does not explain.
specification.successHint: Two deliberately empty fittings are worked into the same shrine mechanism and were made to receive different ceremonial objects.

specification.failureHint: The old residue and wear do not all seem equally old.
specification.successHint: Most wax, soot, and ritual wear are ancient, but several handled surfaces show substantially newer maintenance or contact.

sceneData.name: Central Lodge — C2 Cult Records & Ritual Undercroft

specification.failureHint: Some of the records feel less uniformly old than the room around them.
specification.successHint: Several handled ledgers and writing surfaces show maintenance or use far more recent than the surrounding archive.

specification.failureHint: The archive organization feels deliberately uneven.
specification.successHint: One group of cabinets follows a separate storage logic, as though a category of records was intentionally segregated from the main collection.

sceneData.name: Central Lodge — E1 Arrival Clearing & Front Grounds

intendedBehavior.failureHint: The old hound feels oddly deliberate among the ruin.
intendedBehavior.successHint: One eye is dark stone. The other socket is precisely cut and empty.
intendedBehavior.cooldown: once per character per Scene visit; reset on meaningful puzzle-state change

sceneData.name: Central Lodge — E2 Rear Service Yard & Outbuildings

specification.failureHint: The well's stone rim is more worked than the rest of the yard.
specification.successHint: Several shallow cuts repeat around the well rim in a deliberate sequence.

interpretation.investigation: The cuts form a repeated ordered pattern rather than damage.
interpretation.history: The motif resembles an old estate-maintenance marking convention, but its sequence is unusually deliberate.

behaviorSpec.successMessage: The wear on the old well is not entirely natural. Along the inner stonework, a repeating sequence of deliberately cut marks survives beneath the grime.
behaviorSpec.criticalClueFallback: Deliberate examination of the separate Well Carving Pattern Region remains available.

behaviorSpec.message: Close examination makes the sequence reproducible. You record the Well Carving Pattern for later comparison.

behaviors.name: DiceBox E2 — Well Carving Pattern Recovery

specification.failureHint: Something about the yard's decay feels uneven.
specification.successHint: One wheel rut is sharply edged, and a nearby wood stack has been shifted much more recently than the surrounding rot suggests.
specification.interpretation: The disturbance is recent, but it does not identify who caused it.

behaviorSpec.message: Most of the service yard has settled into years of damp neglect, but this patch has been disturbed much more recently. Something here has been handled or maintained. Nothing about the evidence says who did it.

specification.playerText: Among the old tools is a heavy iron hand crank, still serviceable despite the rust around it.

behaviorSpec.message: Among the old tools is a heavy removable Iron Hand Crank, weathered but still usable.

behaviors.name: DiceBox E2 — Iron Hand Crank Recovery

behaviorSpec.message: The old service hardware includes a detachable Servant Bell Pull. Its fittings suggest it once belonged to a larger bell system inside the Lodge.

behaviors.name: DiceBox E2 — Servant Bell Pull Recovery

behaviorSpec.reason: Destination will be bound by CL-50 after the route table is authoritatively verified.
Destination will be bound by CL-50 after the route table is authoritatively verified.

sceneData.name: Central Lodge — E3 Formal Garden & Greenhouse

behaviorSpec.missingMessage: The sundial's empty center is shaped for a narrow fitted metal piece.
behaviorSpec.successMessage: The Brass Gnomon seats cleanly into the sundial. The mechanism settles into place and a concealed catch beneath the dial releases.

specification.failureHint: The sundial's pedestal has been worked more carefully than the surrounding garden stone.
specification.successHint: The sundial is incomplete: its central fitting is shaped to accept a separate metal piece.

interpretation.investigation: The empty fitting is deliberate and mechanically precise.
interpretation.history: The design is consistent with an estate sundial that once carried a removable gnomon.

behaviorSpec.successMessage: The sundial is incomplete. Its center has a fitted socket where a removable metal gnomon should stand.
behaviorSpec.criticalClueFallback: Deliberate inspection reveals that the sundial is missing a fitted metal gnomon.

specification.failureHint: The fountain's stonework is more complicated than simple plumbing would require.
specification.successHint: Several worn controls and repeated marks around the fountain form an ordered mechanism rather than decoration.

interpretation.investigation: The controls are meant to be operated in a sequence.
interpretation.history: The repeated marks resemble the same estate-era visual language used elsewhere on the grounds.

behaviorSpec.successMessage: The fountain is more mechanism than ornament. Its fittings and channels suggest an ordered control sequence rather than a simple valve.
behaviorSpec.criticalClueFallback: Deliberate inspection reveals that the fountain's controls must be operated in a deliberate sequence.

behaviorSpec.message: You recover the Garden Proof from the neglected garden marker.

behaviors.name: DiceBox E3 Water Control Wheel Installation

behaviorSpec.missingMessage: The fountain assembly has an exposed control spindle, but its wheel is missing.
behaviorSpec.successMessage: The Water Control Wheel from the basement fits the garden mechanism. The control spindle can now be operated.

behaviors.name: DiceBox E3 Fountain Valve Cap Recovery

behaviorSpec.message: Among the greenhouse fittings you recover the Fountain Valve Cap.
You recover the weathered Rose Crest from the garden memorial.

behaviorSpec.incompleteMessage: The fountain mechanism is still incomplete. Its spindle needs its control wheel, one fitting is uncapped, and the correct operating order is not obvious from the mechanism alone.
behaviorSpec.successMessage: Using the Well Carving Pattern as the operating sequence, you seat the Fountain Valve Cap and work the restored control wheel. Water shifts through hidden channels beneath the garden as the fountain mechanism settles into its resolved state.

sceneData.name: Central Lodge — E4 Family Graveyard & Crypt

specification.failureHint: One of the family burials feels wrong in a way that is difficult to place at first glance.
specification.successHint: The stonework and burial arrangement do not agree: this interment was prepared to look complete without being complete.

interpretation.investigation: The physical burial evidence contradicts the appearance of a normal completed interment.
interpretation.history: The memorial treatment is formal, but details of the burial do not match ordinary family practice.

specification.failureHint: Several of the smaller graves have been arranged with unusual care.
specification.successHint: One small burial includes a personal object that does not belong among ordinary grave offerings.

specification.storyEffect: Establishes that at least one formal family burial is incomplete or false without identifying the current cult.

sceneData.name: Central Lodge — M1 Entrance Hall & Great Room

behaviorSpec.message: The Silver Family Emblem fits the clock’s decorative recess exactly. Internal gearing shifts, and the clock face can now be manipulated as part of the mechanism.

specification.failureHint: The room's decay feels uneven in a way you cannot immediately place.
specification.successHint: Dust has been displaced around one chair and side table far more recently than the rest of the room suggests.
specification.interpretation: The disturbance is recent, but nothing here identifies who caused it.

behaviorSpec.successMessage: The decay here is uneven. Dust has been displaced recently, and one piece of furniture appears to have been shifted long after the room was supposedly abandoned. Someone has used this space far more recently than the rest of the Lodge suggests.
behaviorSpec.criticalClueFallback: Deliberate examination of the disturbed area remains possible.

specification.failureHint: The tall clock seems more deliberately built than the other furnishings.
specification.successHint: The clock case has an unusually precise decorative recess and a mechanism that looks incomplete.

interpretation.investigation: The recess is made for a fitted emblem rather than ordinary ornament.
interpretation.history: The clock's decorative program matches the family's heraldic styling.

behaviorSpec.successMessage: The grandfather clock is more deliberately constructed than the surrounding furniture. Part of its ornamentation is missing, leaving a shaped recess connected to the mechanism inside.
behaviorSpec.criticalClueFallback: The clock remains deliberately inspectable even after a failed Notice check.

behaviors.name: DiceBox M1 — Clock Compartment: Reliquary Key

behaviorSpec.message: The concealed clock compartment stands open. Inside is a small Family Reliquary Key.

behaviors.name: DiceBox M1 — Clock Compartment: Baggage Token

behaviorSpec.message: Beside the key rests an old numbered Brass Baggage Token, stamped for the estate railway.

sceneData.name: Central Lodge — M2 Study, Parlor & Formal Rooms

specification.failureHint: One framed family piece draws the eye for reasons that are difficult to place.
specification.successHint: One family portrait has a deliberately altered facial detail and unusually careful framing.

interpretation.investigation: The altered detail is meant to accept a fitted piece rather than being ordinary damage.
interpretation.history: The frame and heraldic motifs belong to the same family program seen elsewhere in the Lodge.

behaviorSpec.successMessage: The founder’s portrait is subtly wrong. One eye does not match the other, and close inspection reveals a fitted recess where a small artificial eye was meant to sit.
behaviorSpec.criticalClueFallback: The portrait remains physically examinable, and the eye mechanism can still be used if the missing Glass Eye is recovered.

behaviorSpec.message: The Glass Eye settles into the altered portrait with a precise mechanical click. The portrait is restored, and something concealed within its construction shifts into a new state.

specification.failureHint: The piano's cabinet work looks more complicated than an ordinary instrument.
specification.successHint: A mechanical feed and concealed access panel mark this as a player piano built to accept a roll.

interpretation.investigation: The mechanism is complete except for the removable music roll.
interpretation.performance: The instrument is designed to perform automatically when its roll mechanism is supplied.

behaviorSpec.successMessage: The player piano is intact, but its mechanism is incomplete. The reader assembly is empty and clearly shaped to accept a perforated music roll.
behaviorSpec.criticalClueFallback: The piano mechanism remains usable if the missing Piano Roll is recovered.

behaviorSpec.message: The Founder’s Signet engages a concealed fitting in the Founder Portrait. A hidden compartment releases, revealing the Old Estate Survey.
You recover the Stag Crest, an old funerary emblem preserved among the Lodge’s formal possessions.
The Piano Roll engages the old mechanism. As the final notes complete, a hidden compartment clicks open and yields a Silver Family Emblem.
The Family Reliquary Key turns in the old lock. Inside rests a carefully wrapped Ceremonial Censer.

sceneData.name: Central Lodge — M3 Kitchen & Service Wing

behaviors.name: DiceBox M3 — Servant Bell Pull Installation

behaviorSpec.missingMessage: The empty fitting beside the servant bell board is missing its pull.
behaviorSpec.successMessage: The Servant Bell Pull fits the weathered bracket. The restored line takes tension, and the bell board mechanism can now respond.

behaviorSpec.message: The resolved bell-board mechanism has exposed a hidden recess containing the Bell Crest.

specification.failureHint: The service wall feels incomplete in a way that is difficult to place.
specification.successHint: The servant bell board has an obvious missing pull or fitting beside its mechanism.

interpretation.investigation: The missing fitting is meant to engage the bell mechanism rather than serve as decoration.

behaviorSpec.successMessage: The servant bell board is incomplete. One line ends at an empty fitting where a pull should attach, and the surrounding mechanism appears designed to respond when that line is restored.
behaviorSpec.criticalClueFallback: Deliberate inspection of the bell board reveals the missing pull-and-fixture relationship.

specification.failureHint: The kitchen's neglect feels uneven.
specification.successHint: A few service objects have been moved much more recently than the surrounding dust suggests.

behaviorSpec.successMessage: The kitchen's neglect is uneven. Dust has been disturbed around a service surface, and a few practical objects were moved recently enough to stand out from the surrounding decay. Someone has used this wing more recently than the rest of the Lodge suggests.
behaviorSpec.criticalClueFallback: Deliberate inspection of the recently disturbed service area remains possible.

sceneData.name: Central Lodge — N1 Underworks Hub / Lodge Railway Station

specification.failureHint: The track margins look more deliberately kept than the rest of the station.
specification.successHint: There is intentional pedestrian clearance beside the rails; the railway was built to be walked as well as ridden.

specification.failureHint: The station hardware seems incomplete rather than simply ruined.
specification.successHint: Three matching authorization points are built into the station controls, each meant to accept a separate proof.

sceneData.name: Central Lodge — N2 Underground Grotto / Garden Station

specification.failureHint: The track bed seems wider and flatter at the edges than a simple rail cut would require.
specification.successHint: Worn foot traffic and deliberate maintenance clearance show that people routinely walked beside the rails.
specification.deliberateInspection: The tunnel-side railway margin is physically traversable on foot.

regions.name: N2 Flood and Drainage Evidence Notice

specification.failureHint: The grotto walls and drains show that the water level has not always stayed where it is now.
specification.successHint: Repeated tide-like staining, drainage hardware, and maintenance marks record cycles of flooding and draining.

dicebox.sourceRegionName: N2 Flood and Drainage Evidence Notice

sceneData.name: Central Lodge — N3 Collection Vaults / Underground Depot

specification.failureHint: One secured storage position is fitted differently from the others.
specification.successHint: A shaped token receiver replaces the ordinary lock hardware on one baggage locker.

specification.failureHint: The turnout mechanism looks maintained rather than abandoned.
specification.successHint: Fresh grease surrounds a keyed spindle where a removable handwheel belongs.

specification.failureHint: Something metallic catches differently among the stored objects.
specification.successHint: A shaped infernal-metal piece matches the other cicada components already recovered.

specification.failureHint: The depot has small inconsistencies in its age and neglect.
specification.successHint: Fresh grease, disturbed dust, newer fasteners, and a recently handled work surface show that someone has used the depot recently.

specification.failureHint: The railway margins are unusually clear for a purely mechanical corridor.
specification.successHint: Continuous pedestrian clearance follows both the main rails and the branch, making the tunnels physically walkable.

specification.failureHint: The mechanical board housing has a deliberate empty interface.
specification.successHint: The empty interface matches the proportions and fittings of a removable route plate.

specification.failureHint: The planning surface has several repeated registration points.
specification.successHint: Three separate overlay positions are designed to align different maps into one route picture.

sceneData.name: Central Lodge — U1 Family & Guest Rooms

behaviorSpec.message: You recover the House Proof from the family wing.
You recover the Crown Crest from the family room.

specification.failureHint: The family papers seem arranged with an odd kind of care.
specification.successHint: A gap and mismatch in the family records suggests that part of the household history has been deliberately separated.

interpretation.investigation: The arrangement preserves chronology while obscuring one branch of the family record.

behaviorSpec.successMessage: The family records are not simply disordered by age. A gap in the sequence and an unusual grouping of names stand out from the surrounding entries, suggesting that part of the household history was organized or omitted deliberately.
behaviorSpec.criticalClueFallback: Deliberate examination of the family records remains possible.

specification.failureHint: One guest room feels strangely incomplete despite being fully furnished.
specification.successHint: The room was prepared for occupation, but the personal traces expected from a long stay are conspicuously absent.

behaviors.name: DiceBox U1 — Guest Room Absence Notice

behaviorSpec.successMessage: One guest room contradicts itself. It is furnished for regular occupation, but the wear, dust, and personal traces expected from a long-term occupant are missing. The absence feels deliberate rather than merely abandoned.
behaviorSpec.criticalClueFallback: Deliberate examination of the room's physical contradictions remains possible.

behaviorSpec.message: Cross-referencing the surviving records establishes a family chronology that connects household generations, the Lodge's genealogy, and the graves outside. It gives context for interpreting the grandfather clock and family memorials, but it does not by itself reveal the clock's exact setting.

sceneData.name: Central Lodge — U2 Servants’ Quarters, Nursery & Attic

specification.failureHint: The small rooms feel oddly stripped of the personal clutter that should have accumulated here.
specification.successHint: Across several rooms, the same kinds of personal belongings are missing, suggesting the absences were systematic rather than accidental.

behaviors.name: DiceBox U2 — Servant Room Absence Notice

behaviorSpec.successMessage: The servants’ rooms are not merely empty. Personal belongings, spare linens, and the ordinary clutter of occupied quarters are missing in a way that suggests the rooms were deliberately cleared rather than simply abandoned.
behaviorSpec.criticalClueFallback: Deliberate examination of the servants’ quarters and the separate Servant History Region remains available.

specification.failureHint: The nursery feels preserved differently from the surrounding service rooms.
specification.successHint: The room's condition does not match the surrounding neglect; a few objects were handled or arranged much later than the rest.

behaviorSpec.successMessage: The nursery has been preserved too carefully. Dust, fading, and age say the room has stood untouched for years, yet several small objects rest as though someone arranged them much more recently. The room’s story does not quite agree with itself.
behaviorSpec.criticalClueFallback: Physical investigation of the nursery and its recoverable objects remains available even if the Notice attempt fails.

behaviorSpec.message: You recover an old but readable Piano Roll. Its perforated pattern was meant for a mechanical instrument elsewhere in the Lodge.
Among the stored household pieces is a removable Brass Gnomon, a shaped pointer from some larger instrument.

Small remnants of the servants’ routine survive in the quarters: wear patterns, old labels, storage habits, and the careful organization of people expected to keep a large household running. Whatever ended that routine did so with unnerving completeness.
You recover a small artificial Glass Eye, intact despite the years of neglect.
